subject: scorpion
pitch: A desert scorpion in a threatening pose, tail arched high over its back. Glossy amber armour with darker bands at every joint, big crab-like pincers held forward, eight thin legs, a segmented tail ending in a bulbous dark stinger, and a cluster of tiny black eyes on the head shield.
reasoning:
I'm planning out realistic scorpion proportions for the module, aiming for roughly 0.14 m total length and about 0.1 m height with the tail arched, based on desert scorpion species sizes.

Now I'm designing the skeleton structure: a root body joint positioned above the floor so legs reach down to touch it, with separate chains for the legs, tail, and pincers branching from the body. I'm defining the pincer arm as a chain extending forward and outward from the prosoma to form the claw.

Writing joint path data...

I'm planning eight legs with four z-positions relative to the body, building a helper function to generate each leg chain with proper side naming. Then I'm setting up the pincer "arm" chain and starting the tail chain, which arches upward from the rear of the body over the back.

Now I'm refining the tail geometry into five tapering segments with a stinger joint, planning darker bands along the metasoma using color functions for an amber glossy armor look.

Simplifying further: instead of discrete bands, I'll drive color through a periodic function of t that darkens near each segment boundary, letting the renderer bisect exactly where the color shifts so joints read as darker rings without manual band lists.

Since paint colors give matte roughness anyway and I can't control glossiness directly, I'll approximate gloss visually through color variation rather than material properties — maybe using a mottle paint on the carapace and body for texture instead of flat color strings.

Now I'm sketching the body shapes: the prosoma as a lofted blob with stations defining width and height along the z-axis, trying to get the flattened scorpion head-thorax silhouette right before moving to the rest of the segments.

Adding more loft stations...

I'll pass the bone explicitly to the loft call to avoid relying on nearest-joint inference. For the head shield, I'm considering a flattened sphere scaled non-uniformly in x/y/z to form the prosoma cap shape, using the part scale option.

For the eyes, I'm calculating the positions of a small cluster of tiny dark spheres sitting on top of the shield's ellipsoid surface, working out the approximate y and z offsets based on the shield's scaled radius so the eyes sit correctly on the curved surface.

For the eye geometry I'll use a small sphere with few segments for a faceted look. Then I'm planning the pincer arm chain as a sequence of joints—shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip—forming a crab-like pedipalp with a bulky claw at the end, building it segment by segment with varying thickness.

Still working out the claw...

Setting up the rod geometry for the finger, with radius tapering and bone-weighting tied to the fingerL joint. Now I'm adding the stinger: a bulbous dark tip at the tail's end, with the sweep radius function expanding near the tail's final segment to form the bulb shape.

Defining tail chain points...

Switching to catmull-spline for the tail gives smooth knots at each point rather than polyline kinks, and with 6 control points I get 5 spans plus a tip, matching the chain's expected segment count.

Now I'm sweeping the tail tube along this chain with a radius function of t, keeping a single smooth mesh skin. For the dark bands, I'm computing a periodic function of t so that near each joint (every 1/5 of arc length) the color shifts to a darker tone, otherwise amber.

Knots roughly correspond to joint cut points, and with ~10 color splits the mesh will segment into separate pieces, which is acceptable. I'm settling on a color palette: glossy amber for armor, deep brown for bands, near-black for stinger and eyes, a touch darker amber for legs, and a lighter amber shield tone — possibly mottling the carapace surface for texture.

For the body surface I'm applying a mottled texture on the loft, then layering ring-like stripes along the z-axis to create segmented dark bands around the abdomen at each joint, using amber as the base and dark brown as the stripe color with some wobble for a natural look.

For legs, I'm defining each as a four-point chain—hip, knee, ankle, foot—swept with a tapering radius so the leg narrows toward the tip, positioning the foot just above ground level so it touches down. I'm checking that hip joints sit close enough to the body to look attached without obviously clipping through it.

I'm deciding to use polyline chains rather than smooth curves so the legs have an angular, bent-joint look characteristic of crab legs, and I'm setting up a staggered z-position array for the four leg pairs along the body with slight offsets at each joint so they splay naturally outward.

Now I'm laying out the pincer/claw as a short chain of points from shoulder through elbow and wrist to the hand tip, giving each joint a unique name so the arm segments render distinctly, and tapering the sweep radius slightly from the forearm down to the wrist for a more natural pincer shape.

Adding the claw hand and fingers...

Marking "spine" as optional for the body joint. I'm checking whether root needs explicit joint attachment points, then sketching the shield as a small sphere using the segments helper for geometry detail, moving next to the ellipsoid shape.

I'm positioning the shield at the head front, checking it sits properly atop the body loft without clipping awkwardly, and picking a darker amber color for the shield paint. Now I'm placing the eyes on the shield.

For each eye I'm finding the nearest point on the shield surface and attaching a tiny dark sphere embedded slightly into it, oriented to aim along the surface normal, using low-poly geometry since the eyes are so small. I'm computing eye positions along the shield's upper-front ellipsoid curve, mapping out roughly eight symmetric points to project onto the surface.

Then I'm moving on to the stinger at the tail tip, planning to base it off the end of the tail's catmull-rom path with a direction derived from the tail's tangent there, figuring out the bulb radius near the tip.

Tweaking the bulb radius profile near the tip and picking the stinger base point from the tail chain around t=0.96-0.97, using a frame reference for the spike's base position.

I'm working out the direction vector for the stinger so it points forward and slightly downward, matching the tail's curve as it arcs over the body, letting the spike function handle normalization and weight inheritance from the chain joint.

For color, I'm setting up a banding function where most of the tail alternates dark bands at joints with amber segments, but the last stretch near t=0.84 switches entirely to a dark stinger color. For radius, I'm tapering the tail thickness down linearly while adding a bulb-shaped bump near the tip using a Gaussian falloff centered around t=0.9 to create that bulbous stinger base.

I'm positioning the tail's starting point just inside the rear of the body loft, confirming it fits the body's geometry at that station. I'm also naming the chain bones for the tail segments, ending in a "stinger" joint as the tip.

Naming legs and limb chains...

Sweeping the arms with a shrinking radius for taper, using catmull-rom through four points per limb, and tagging joint roles like leg/arm/tail for later reference. I should double check leg geometry actually touches the ground plane so foot contact looks right.

Adjusting foot y-position so the bottommost sweep point slightly penetrates y=0 rather than floating above it, keeping contact believable. The prosoma body sits well clear of the floor, so the legs remain the true lowest points of the whole model, which is what I want.

Setting up the body joint as the root at (0, 0.03, 0) with no parent, then starting the loft bone for the torso. Checking overall proportions—tail to pincer span around 0.2m, a bit large for a real scorpion but reasonable for a stylized model.

Writing the TypeScript module imports and color palette constants...

Still writing loft stations...

I'm checking that the body station widths and heights look proportional, with the front station tapering appropriately and the shield-like segment near the top sitting correctly. The hip placement on the legs looks like it stays within the body bounds, so the overall structure seems consistent.

Now I'm working out the spider's shield piece—a flattened sphere positioned toward the front of the prosoma and rigidly attached to the body bone, checking that its scale keeps it sitting mostly above the body without poking out awkwardly. Then I'm placing the eight eyes as small spheres across the front of the shield, spacing them in a typical jumping-spider arrangement with a central pair, side pairs, and smaller posterior eyes.

I'm deciding each eye should probably get its own geometry instance rather than sharing one, just to be safe with how the mesh transforms and bounding boxes get computed, even though sharing would technically still render correctly since each eye gets positioned via its own transform.

Now I'm working out the leg placement for all four legs, computing hip, knee, ankle, and foot points with z-offsets so the front legs lean forward and back legs lean backward, using a lean array to control how much each joint shifts along z.

Setting up chain code...

Still defining the tail chain...

Adding tail color logic...

Checking the banding formula: at t=0 the modulo is 0, so dark right at the joint start, and the dark band spans a short interval right after each joint — that matches the intended look of dark markers after joints.

Now I'm adding a stinger spike positioned near the tail tip, angled forward-down over the body for a menacing look, making sure to reference the tail's tip joint correctly for the bone attachment. Writing the pincer loop code...

Adding the fixed finger rod geometry now...

Adding finger bone and rod definitions...

I'll skip the fingertip detail and dorsal ridge additions to keep things simple, and just make sure the stripes paint function works for the loft color.

Now I'm finalizing the return statement and export structure, trimming unused imports like rng and mottle, and double-checking type compatibility for the leg path arrays and pincer points through catmull. I'm also verifying the eye stick geometry hits the nearest surface point correctly.

Working out leg hip positions, lean offsets, and foot placement for left/right symmetry...
